/-!
# Erdős Problem 546

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/546](https://www.erdosproblems.com/546)
- [Su11] Sudakov, B., A conjecture of Erdős on graph Ramsey numbers. Adv. Math. (2011), 3148-3155.
- [AKS03] Alon, N., Krivelevich, M. and Sudakov, B., Turán numbers of bipartite graphs and Ramsey
  graphs of bounded degree. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2003), 477-483.
-/

namespace Erdos546

/--
Let $G$ be a graph with no isolated vertices and $m$ edges. Is it true that
$$R(G) \leq 2^{O(m^{1/2})}?$$

This is true, and was proved by Sudakov [Su11].

This problem is #11 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_546 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (m : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      (∀ v, 0 < G.degree v) →
      G.edgeSet.ncard = m →
      (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey G : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ (C * Real.sqrt m) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos546

findings.description: The [Su11] reference on line 24 gives the wrong page range, 3148–3155. The cited paper was published in Advances in Mathematics 227 (2011), 601–609. This does not affect the mathematical statement.
findings.source_evidence: The first page of Sudakov's published paper reads “Advances in Mathematics 227 (2011) 601–609”: https://www.math.ethz.ch/~sudakovb/erdos-ramsey-problem.pdf. The author's publication list gives the same citation.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct [Su11] to: Sudakov, B., A conjecture of Erdős on graph Ramsey numbers. Adv. Math. 227 (2011), 601–609.

findings.description: The [AKS03] reference on lines 25–26 has an incorrect title and page range. The intended paper is “Turán numbers of bipartite graphs and related Ramsey-type questions,” pp. 477–494, not “Turán numbers of bipartite graphs and Ramsey graphs of bounded degree,” pp. 477–483.
findings.source_evidence: The published paper's first page gives the title “Turán Numbers of Bipartite Graphs and Related Ramsey-Type Questions” and “Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (2003) 12, 477–494”: https://www.math.ethz.ch/~sudakovb/bipartite-turan-numbers.pdf. Its Conjecture 5.1 is precisely the conjecture formalized here.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct [AKS03] to: Alon, N., Krivelevich, M. and Sudakov, B., Turán numbers of bipartite graphs and related Ramsey-type questions. Combin. Probab. Comput. 12 (2003), 477–494.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1002.0095 — Sudakov, introduction, Theorem 1.1, proof and concluding remarks
https://www.math.ethz.ch/~sudakovb/bipartite-turan-numbers.pdf — introduction, Conjecture 5.1, related results in Section 5, and concluding remarks
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in Erdos546.erdos_546. AKS Conjecture 5.1 explicitly asks for an absolute c > 0 valid for every graph with m edges and no isolated vertices. Sudakov's Theorem 1.1 proves the bound with c = 250, supporting answer(True) and research solved. The imported Ramsey definition uses ordinary, not induced, copies; finite Ramsey existence prevents its empty-infimum default from affecting the claim. Edge cardinality counts unordered edges, and positive degree is exactly non-isolation. Independent Lean checks in /workspace/review/checked.lean verified these degree equivalences, the zero-edge/no-isolates boundary, Ramsey number 0 for an empty vertex type, and Ramsey number 2 for K₂; the named boundary proofs have no sorry axioms. The live erdosproblems.com page repeatedly returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its latest remarks and the ancillary '#11' collection locator were not directly checked. The mathematical statement and solved status were verified against both cited primary papers.
